title: Excursion-boat bands out of St. Louis: Bix, Trumbauer, Louis
summary: He grew up hearing bands on riverboat excursions, including early Bix Beiderbecke, Frankie Trumbauer, Ray Ludwig and Louis Armstrong, and says St. Louis was a hub of jazz.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Just improvising. And then the river boats, you see, I heard -- I grew up listening to all the bands on the riverboats, like I first heard Bix Beiderbecke and Frankie Trumbauer and Ray Ludwig and all these fellas out of St. Louis, cause at that time, in well -- say 1908, by 1918, around
there, St. Louis was really the hub of jazz, more than people really give credit for.
Yeah.
That's where Louis was. I heard Louis on the boats. In those early years --
Did you, really?
-- in the '20's, too, because see the excursion boats would come out of St. Louis. They'd go up and down the Mississippi and the Illinois and all these rivers.
Yeah.
And during the summertime in my hometown that was a big thing. They didn't have a dance hall here --
Yeah.
-- all the dancing was done on the excursion boats.
Yeah, I see.

Say a department store, like Kleins Department Store, if you traded there they'd have an all-day excursion, go down the locks, down to the Meredosia and you'd get on 8:00 in the morning and in the afternoon the band would play, --
Well when did the band come off, same time as you did? I mean would they go --
No, they lived -- they lived on the boat.
Oh, they lived --
Yeah, they lived, that was a job. They lived on the boat.
Oh.
They stayed on that boat. They were hired for the summer --
Oh, I see.
-- or for that time. The job was there. They had -- cabins --
Oh, they did?
-- just like the Captain, and the crew.
Is that right?

And the piano player would go up and play the calliope. When the boat would dock, like if it was a moonlight excursion -- say it left at 8:00 o'clock, well at 7:30, you -- all over the town you'd hear that calliope --
I see.
-- and then he would be playing tunes up on the calliope. That was the signal, sure.
